figures.finding: Riga City Council's Riga Film Fund pays Latvian-foreign co-productions shooting in Riga and Latvia a cash rebate of up to 25% of eligible film-related expenditure once filming is completed, and can be combined with the co-financing the National Film Centre of Latvia administers (whose current terms could not be read; see blockers).

figures.finding: Latvia's film industry counts 195 registered film producers and studios (city agency, 2026); in 2014 annual state support for film was EUR 4,041,639, only three Latvian features premiered in 2013 and six releases were expected in 2014, most of them co-productions.
figures.applies: Latvia; producer count 2026, funding and releases 2013-2014 (FNE, citing the period's figures).

sources.said: There are 195 registered film producers and studios represented in the industry.

The annual state support for film industry in 2014 is 4,041,639 EUR, which is over 1m EUR more than in 2013. … Although only three features premiered in 2013 … Six films will be released in 2014 … Most of the feature films released are coproductions

figures.finding: Latvia's National Film Centre funds new films by annual production competition: in 2022, 41 projects asked for EUR 6,672,951 and 16 were funded from EUR 1,982,472 (five features EUR 1,209,046, seven documentaries EUR 414,790, four animations EUR 358,636), a selection rate of about 39%.

sources.said: Nacionālajā Kino centrā noslēdzies 2022. gada jaunu filmu ražošanas konkurss ar pieejamo finansējumu EUR 1 982 472 ; atbalstīti 16 filmu projekti – piecas spēlfilmas, septiņas dokumentālās filmas un četras animācijas filmas. … konkursam tika iesniegts kopā 41 projekts, kopējais projektos pieprasītā finansējuma apjoms bija EUR 6 672 951. … No konkursā pieejamā finansējuma spēlfilmām tiks piešķirti EUR 1 209 046 (piecu pilnmetrāžas filmu ražošanas uzsākšanai), dokumentālajām filmām EUR 414 790 (septiņām dažāda garuma filmām) un animācijas filmām EUR 358 636
